verses.1:1: Now King David was old, advanced in years; and they covered him with garments, yet he could not get warm.
verses.1:2: Therefore his servants said to him, "Let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin, and let her stand before the king and be his attendant; and let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may be warm."
verses.1:3: So they sought a fair young woman throughout all the territory of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
verses.1:4: And the young woman was exceedingly fair, and she became an attendant to the king and ministered to him; yet the king did not know her.
verses.1:5: Now Adonijah the son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying, "I will reign!" And he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.1:6: And his father had never displeased him in all his days by saying, "Why have you done thus?" Moreover, he was also exceedingly handsome in form, and his mother had borne him after Absalom.
verses.1:7: And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest; and they followed and aided Adonijah.
verses.1:8: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men who belonged to David were not with Adonijah.
verses.1:9: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and oxen and fattened cattle by the Stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En Rogel; and he invited all his brethren, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.
verses.1:10: Yet Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother he did not invite.
verses.1:11: Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, "Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has become king, and David our lord does not know it?
verses.1:12: Now therefore, come, please let me give you counsel, that you may deliver your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
verses.1:13: Go and enter in to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your maidservant, saying, "Surely Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
verses.1:14: Behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I also will come in after you and confirm your words."
verses.1:15: So Bathsheba went in to the king into the chamber. Now the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was ministering to the king.
verses.1:16: And Bathsheba bowed and paid homage to the king. Then the king said, "What is your desire?"
verses.1:17: And she said to him, "My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your maidservant, 'Surely Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne.'
verses.1:18: And now, behold, Adonijah has become king; and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.
verses.1:19: He has sacrificed oxen and fattened cattle and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army; yet Solomon your servant he has not invited.
verses.1:20: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you, that you should declare to them who shall sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him.
verses.1:21: Otherwise it shall come to pass, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be counted as offenders."
verses.1:22: And behold, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
verses.1:23: And they told the king, saying, "Behold, Nathan the prophet!" And when he came in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.
verses.1:24: Then Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne'?
verses.1:25: For he has gone down this day and has sacrificed oxen and fattened cattle and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the sons of the king, and the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest; and behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and saying, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
verses.1:26: Yet me—even me, your servant—and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant he has not invited.
verses.1:27: Has this thing come about from my lord the king, and you have not made known to your servant who shall sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him?"
verses.1:28: Then King David answered and said, "Call Bathsheba to me." So she came into the king's presence and stood before the king.
verses.1:29: And the king swore and said, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
verses.1:30: even as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, 'Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead,' surely so I will do this very day."
verses.1:31: Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and paid homage to the king, and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
verses.1:32: And King David said, "Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada." So they came before the king.
verses.1:33: And the king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
verses.1:34: And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel; and blow the trumpet and say, 'Long live King Solomon!'
verses.1:35: Then you shall come up after him, and he shall enter and sit upon my throne, for he shall reign in my stead; and him I have appointed to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."
verses.1:36: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so as well!
verses.1:37: As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."
verses.1:38: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down and caused Solomon to ride upon King David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.
verses.1:39: Then Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"
verses.1:40: And all the people went up after him, and the people were playing on pipes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth split open at their sound.
verses.1:41: Now Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. And when Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "Why is the sound of the city in an uproar?"
verses.1:42: While he was still speaking, behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came in. And Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a worthy man and bring good tidings."
verses.1:43: Then Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, "No indeed! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
verses.1:44: And the king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride upon the king's mule.
verses.1:45: And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon; and they have gone up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. That is the sound which you have heard.
verses.1:46: Moreover, Solomon has taken his seat upon the throne of the kingdom.
verses.1:47: And the king's servants also came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May God make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne!' And the king bowed himself upon the bed.
verses.1:48: And thus also the king spoke, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has given one to sit upon my throne this day, while my eyes see it.'"
verses.1:49: Then all the guests who were with Adonijah trembled and rose up, and each man went his own way.
verses.1:50: And Adonijah feared because of Solomon; so he arose, and went, and took hold of the horns of the altar.
verses.1:51: And it was told Solomon, saying, "Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon; and behold, he has laid hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me this day that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"
verses.1:52: And Solomon said, "If he proves himself a worthy man, not a hair of his shall fall to the ground; but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die."
verses.1:53: So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself before King Solomon; and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
verses.2:1: Now the days of David drew near that he should die, and he charged Solomon his son, saying,
verses.2:2: "I am going the way of all the earth; therefore be strong, and be a man.
verses.2:3: Keep the charge of the LORD your God, to walk in His ways and to observe His statutes, His commandments, His judgments, and His testimonies, as it is written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in everything you do and in whatever direction you turn,
verses.2:4: that the LORD may establish His word which He spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons guard their way, to walk before Me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul,' saying, 'a man shall not be cut off from you from the throne of Israel.'
verses.2:5: Moreover, you yourself know what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, and what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner the son of Ner and to Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, shedding the blood of war in peace and putting the blood of war upon the belt around his waist and upon the sandals on his feet.
verses.2:6: Act therefore according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray hair go down in peace to Sheol.
verses.2:7: But show lovingkindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table; for in this way they drew near to me when I fled before Absalom your brother.
verses.2:8: And behold, you have with you Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day I went to Mahanaim; yet he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
verses.2:9: Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man, and you know what you should do to him; bring his gray hair down to Sheol with blood."
verses.2:10: Then David slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the City of David.
verses.2:11: And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years he reigned in Hebron, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.
verses.2:12: Then Solomon sat upon the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was very firmly established.
verses.2:13: Now Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, "Do you come in peace?" And he said, "In peace."
verses.2:14: Moreover he said, "I have a word for you." And she said, "Speak."
verses.2:15: Then he said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel had set their faces upon me to reign; yet the kingdom has turned about and become my brother's, for it was his from the LORD.
verses.2:16: And now I ask one petition of you; do not turn me away." And she said to him, "Speak."
verses.2:17: So he said, "Please speak to King Solomon, for he will not turn you away, that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife."
verses.2:18: And Bathsheba said, "Very well; I will speak for you to the king."
verses.2:19: Therefore Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonijah. And the king rose to meet her and bowed down before her; then he sat upon his throne and had a throne placed for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
verses.2:20: Then she said, "I ask one small petition of you; do not turn me away." And the king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not turn you away."
verses.2:21: So she said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as a wife."
verses.2:22: And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, "Why then do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him also, for he is my elder brother—for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah!"
verses.2:23: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, "May God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word against his own life!
verses.2:24: Now therefore, as the LORD lives, who has established me and seated me upon the throne of my father David, and who has made a house for me as He spoke, Adonijah shall surely be put to death today!"
verses.2:25: So King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he struck him down, and he died.
verses.2:26: And to Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your own fields, for you are a man deserving of death; yet on this day I will not put you to death, because you bore the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and because you were afflicted in everything in which my father was afflicted."
verses.2:27: So Solomon expelled Abiathar from being priest to the LORD, in order to fulfill the word of the LORD which He spoke concerning the house of Eli at Shiloh.
verses.2:28: Then the report came to Joab, for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he had not turned after Absalom. And Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
verses.2:29: And it was told to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD, and behold, he was beside the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike him down."
verses.2:30: So Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, "Thus says the king, 'Come out!'" And he said, "No, for I will die here." Then Benaiah brought back word to the king, saying, "Thus spoke Joab, and thus he answered me."
verses.2:31: And the king said to him, "Do as he has spoken, and strike him down and bury him, that you may remove from me and from my father's house the innocent blood which Joab shed.
verses.2:32: Thus the LORD shall bring his blood back upon his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he, and slew them with the sword while my father David did not know it—Abner the son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.
verses.2:33: Their blood shall therefore return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his descendants forever; but upon David and his descendants, upon his house and his throne, there shall be peace forever from the LORD."
verses.2:34: So Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up and struck him down and put him to death, and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
verses.2:35: Then the king appointed Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and the king appointed Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar. These were the chief officers who were over Solomon's work: five hundred and fifty who ruled over the people doing the work. And three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar which he had built to the LORD, and he burned incense beside it, which was before the LORD. So he finished the house.
verses.2:36: Then the king sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere.
verses.2:37: For it shall be, on the day you go out and cross over the Brook Kidron, know for certain that you shall surely die; your blood shall be upon your own head."
verses.2:38: And Shimei said to the king, "The word is good. As my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do." So Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.
verses.2:39: Now it came to pass at the end of three years that two of Shimei's servants fled to Achish the son of Maacah, king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, "Behold, your servants are in Gath."
verses.2:40: So Shimei arose, saddled his donkey, and went to Gath to Achish to seek his servants; and Shimei went and brought his servants from Gath.
verses.2:41: And it was reported to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.
verses.2:42: Then the king sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and solemnly warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and walk anywhere, know for certain that you shall surely die'? And you said to me, 'The word is good; I have heard it.'
verses.2:43: Why then have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the commandment which I laid upon you?"
verses.2:44: The king also said to Shimei, "You know all the evil, which your own heart knows, that you did to my father David; therefore the LORD shall return your evil upon your own head.
verses.2:45: But King Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the LORD forever."
verses.2:46: So the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon. Judah and Israel were many, as the sand by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing. And Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines, and as far as the border of Egypt; they brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life. And Judah and Israel dwelt securely, each man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
verses.3:2: Only the people were offering sacrifices at the high places, for no house had been built for the name of the LORD until those days.
verses.3:3: Now Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of his father David; only he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
verses.3:4: And the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place; Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings upon that altar.
verses.3:5: In Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; and God said, "Ask what I shall give you."
verses.3:6: And Solomon said, "You have shown great lovingkindness to Your servant my father David, as he walked before You in truth, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with You; and You have preserved for him this great lovingkindness, and have given him a son sitting upon his throne, as it is this day.
verses.3:7: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in place of my father David; yet I am but a little youth; I do not know how to go out or come in.
verses.3:8: And Your servant is in the midst of Your people whom You have chosen, a vast people who cannot be numbered or counted for multitude.
verses.3:9: Give therefore to Your servant a listening heart to judge Your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of Yours?"
verses.3:10: And the matter was pleasing in the sight of the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.
verses.3:11: Then God said to him, "Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked many days for yourself, nor have asked wealth for yourself, nor have asked the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself discernment to hear justice,
verses.3:12: behold, I have acted according to your words; behold, I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that none like you has been before you, nor after you shall any arise like you.
verses.3:13: And what you have not asked I have also given you, both riches and honor, so that no man among the kings shall be like you all your days.
verses.3:14: And if you walk in My ways, keeping My statutes and My commandments, as your father David walked, then I will lengthen your days."
verses.3:15: Then Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. And he came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings and presented peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
verses.3:16: Then two women who were harlots came to the king and stood before him.
verses.3:17: And the one woman said, "O my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house, and I gave birth while with her in the house.
verses.3:18: And it came to pass on the third day after I gave birth that this woman also gave birth. And we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, only the two of us in the house.
verses.3:19: And this woman's son died in the night, because she lay upon him.
verses.3:20: So she arose in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while your maidservant slept, and laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead son in my bosom.
verses.3:21: And when I arose in the morning to nurse my son, behold, he was dead; yet when I looked closely at him in the morning, behold, it was not my son whom I had borne."
verses.3:22: Then the other woman said, "No! Rather, my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one." And the first said, "No! Rather, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one." Thus they spoke before the king.
verses.3:23: And the king said, "This one says, 'This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one'; and that one says, 'No! Rather, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.'"
verses.3:24: Then the king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought the sword before the king.
verses.3:25: And the king said, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other."
verses.3:26: Then the woman whose son was the living one spoke to the king, for her compassion burned within her for her son, and she said, "O my lord, give her the living babe, and by no means slay him!" But the other said, "He shall be neither mine nor yours; divide him!"
verses.3:27: So the king answered and said, "Give her the living babe, and by no means slay him; she is his mother."
verses.3:28: And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had rendered, and they stood in awe before the king; for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to execute justice.
verses.4:1: So King Solomon was king over all Israel.
verses.4:2: And these were the officials whom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok, the priest;
verses.4:3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder;
verses.4:4: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
verses.4:5: Azariah the son of Nathan, over the deputies; Zabud the son of Nathan, a priest, the king's friend;
verses.4:6: Ahishar, over the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda, over the forced labor.
verses.4:7: And Solomon had twelve deputies over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household; each one had to provide for one month in the year.
verses.4:8: And these are their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
verses.4:9: Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan;
verses.4:10: Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth; to him belonged Sochoh and all the land of Hepher;
verses.4:11: Ben-Abinadab, in all the region of Dor; Taphath the daughter of Solomon was his wife;
verses.4:12: Baana the son of Ahilud, in Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth Shean, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shean to Abel Meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;
verses.4:13: Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead; to him belonged the villages of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead; to him also belonged the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars;
verses.4:14: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
verses.4:15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he also took Basemath the daughter of Solomon as his wife;
verses.4:16: Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and in Aloth;
verses.4:17: Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
verses.4:18: Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and he was the one deputy who was in the land;
verses.4:19: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar.
verses.5:1: And these officers provided sustenance for King Solomon and for all who came to the table of King Solomon, each man in his month; they let nothing be lacking. Also barley and straw for the horses and the swift steeds they brought to the place where he was, each man according to his appointed charge.
verses.5:2: Now Solomon's provision for one day was thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of meal,
verses.5:3: ten fattened oxen, twenty oxen from the pasture, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.
verses.5:4: For he held dominion over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River; and he had peace on every side all around him.
verses.5:9: And God gave Solomon wisdom and exceedingly great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand that is upon the seashore.
verses.5:10: And the wisdom of Solomon surpassed the wisdom of all the sons of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt.
verses.5:11: For he was wiser than all mankind—than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his fame was in all the nations round about.
verses.5:12: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered one thousand and five.
verses.5:13: He also spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that springs forth out of the wall; and he spoke of beasts, and of birds, and of creeping things, and of fish.
verses.5:14: Now Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took the daughter of Pharaoh and brought her into the City of David until he had finished building his own house, and the house of the LORD, and the wall of Jerusalem round about. And people came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom. Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up and captured Gezer and burned it with fire, and had slain the Canaanites who dwelt in the city, and had given it as a dowry to his daughter, the wife of Solomon.
verses.5:15: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father; for Hiram had always been a friend to David.
verses.5:16: Then Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying,
verses.5:17: "You know concerning my father David, that he was unable to build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the warfare that surrounded him, until the LORD placed them beneath the soles of my feet.
verses.5:18: But now the LORD my God has granted me rest on every side; there is neither adversary nor evil occurrence.
verses.5:19: And behold, I purpose to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD spoke to my father David, saying, 'Your son, whom I will set upon your throne in your place, he shall build the house for My name.'
verses.5:20: Now therefore, give command that they cut down cedars for me out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be with your servants, and I will give you wages for your servants according to all that you say, for you know that there is no man among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."
verses.5:21: And it came to pass, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced exceedingly and said, "Blessed be the LORD this day, who has given to David a wise son over this great people."
verses.5:22: Then Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, "I have heard what you sent to me; I will fulfill all your desire concerning timber of cedar and timber of cypress.
verses.5:23: My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will set them in rafts upon the sea to the place of which you send word to me, and I will break them apart there, and you shall take them away; and you shall fulfill my desire by giving food for my household."
verses.5:24: So Hiram supplied Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber according to all his desire.
verses.5:25: And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty kors of beaten oil; thus Solomon gave to Hiram year by year.
verses.5:26: And the LORD gave wisdom to Solomon, just as He had promised him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.
verses.5:27: Then King Solomon raised a levy of forced labor out of all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.
verses.5:28: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in shifts: one month they were in Lebanon and two months at home; and Adoniram was over the levy.
verses.5:29: Solomon also had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
verses.5:30: besides the chief officers of Solomon who were over the work, three thousand three hundred, who had charge over the people carrying out the work.
verses.5:32: So the builders of Solomon and the builders of Hiram and the Gebalites did the hewing, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.
verses.6:1: And the king commanded, and they quarried great stones, costly stones, hewn stones, to lay the foundation of the house. And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, that he began to build the house for the LORD. In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv. And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was completed in all its parts and according to all its specifications; thus he was seven years in building it.
verses.6:2: Now the house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits in length, twenty in width, and thirty cubits in height.
verses.6:3: And the vestibule in front of the sanctuary of the house was twenty cubits in length across the width of the house, and ten cubits in width in front of the house.
verses.6:4: And he made for the house windows with recessed frames.
verses.6:5: Against the wall of the house he built a side structure all around, against the walls of the house all around, both of the sanctuary and of the inner sanctuary; and he made side chambers all around.
verses.6:6: The lowest story of the side structure was five cubits wide, the middle was six cubits wide, and the third was seven cubits wide; for on the outside of the house he made recessed ledges all around, so that the beams would not be fastened into the walls of the house.
verses.6:7: And the house, while it was being built, was built of finished stone dressed at the quarry, so that neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard in the house while it was being built.
verses.6:8: The entrance to the middle side chamber was on the right side of the house; and they went up by winding stairs to the middle story, and from the middle to the third.
verses.6:9: So he built the house and finished it, and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.
verses.6:10: And he built the side structure against the entire house, five cubits in height, and it was fastened to the house with timbers of cedar.
verses.6:15: And he lined the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the beams of the ceiling he paneled them on the inside with wood, and he overlaid the floor of the house with planks of cypress.
verses.6:16: And he built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with boards of cedar from the floor to the rafters; he built it on the inside as an inner sanctuary, as the Most Holy Place.
verses.6:17: And the house—that is, the sanctuary in front—was forty cubits long.
verses.6:19: And he prepared the inner sanctuary in the innermost part of the house, to set there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
verses.6:20: And the interior of the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in height; and he overlaid it with pure gold, and he overlaid the cedar altar.
verses.6:21: So Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold; and he drew chains of gold across before the inner sanctuary, and overlaid it with gold.
verses.6:22: The whole house he overlaid with gold, until the entire house was finished; also the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.
verses.6:23: Within the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits in height.
verses.6:24: One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits; ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
verses.6:25: And the second cherub was also ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measure and the same form.
verses.6:26: The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and likewise that of the second cherub.
verses.6:27: Then he set the cherubim inside the inner house; and the wings of the cherubim were spread out so that the wing of the one touched one wall, and the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and their wings toward the middle of the house touched wing to wing.
verses.6:28: And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
verses.6:29: And all the walls of the house round about he carved with engraved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, both in the inner and the outer rooms.
verses.6:30: And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, both in the inner and the outer rooms.
verses.6:31: And for the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the lintel and doorposts were five-sided.
verses.6:32: The two doors were of olive wood, and he carved upon them carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold; and he beat out the gold over the cherubim and over the palm trees.
verses.6:33: In like manner he made for the entrance of the sanctuary four-sided doorposts of olive wood,
verses.6:34: and two doors of cypress wood; the two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the second door were folding.
verses.6:35: And he carved upon them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold smoothly fitted upon the carved work.
verses.6:36: And he built the inner court with three courses of hewn stone and a course of cedar beams.
verses.7:1: And King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.
verses.7:2: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze; he was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to perform every kind of work in bronze. So he came to King Solomon and accomplished all his work.
verses.7:3: He cast the two pillars of bronze: eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and a cord of twelve cubits encompassed the second pillar.
verses.7:4: And he made two capitals of molten bronze to set upon the tops of the pillars: five cubits was the height of the one capital, and five cubits was the height of the second capital.
verses.7:5: There were networks of latticework and wreaths of chainwork for the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars: seven for the one capital, and seven for the second capital.
verses.7:6: So he made the pillars, with two rows all around upon the one network to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates, and thus he did for the second capital. And the capitals upon the two pillars were also above, opposite the rounded bulge that was beside the network; and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows all around upon the second capital.
verses.7:7: Then he set up the pillars for the porch of the temple: he set up the right pillar and called its name Jachin, and he set up the left pillar and called its name Boaz.
verses.7:8: And the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars in the porch were of lily work, four cubits. And upon the top of the pillars was lily work; thus the work of the pillars was finished.
verses.7:10: And he made the molten Sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, completely round; its height was five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits encompassed it all around.
verses.7:11: Beneath its brim all around were gourds encircling it, ten to a cubit, surrounding the Sea all around; the gourds were in two rows, cast together in its casting.
verses.7:12: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom; it held two thousand baths.
verses.7:13: It stood upon twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east; the Sea was set upon them above, and all their hinder parts were turned inward.
verses.7:14: He also made the ten stands of bronze: four cubits was the length of each stand, four cubits its width, and three cubits its height.
verses.7:15: And this was the workmanship of the stands: they had panels, and panels were between the frames.
verses.7:16: Upon the panels that were between the frames were lions, oxen, and cherubim, and upon the frames there was a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and the oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
verses.7:17: Each stand had four bronze wheels and axles of bronze, and its four feet had supports; beneath the laver the supports were cast, with wreaths beside each one.
verses.7:18: Its opening was within the crown and rose upward by a cubit; its opening was round, of pedestal workmanship, a cubit and a half, and upon its opening also were engravings, while their panels were square, not round. And the four wheels were beneath the panels, and the axletrees of the wheels were attached to the stand; and the height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
verses.7:19: The workmanship of the wheels was like the workmanship of a chariot wheel: their axletrees, their rims, their spokes, and their hubs were all cast.
verses.7:20: There were four supports at the four corners of each stand; its supports were of one piece with the stand itself.
verses.7:21: And at the top of the stand was a band half a cubit high, round all around; and on the top of the stand, its stays and its panels were of one piece with it.
verses.7:22: On the plates of its stays and on its panels he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, according to the clear space of each, with wreaths all around.
verses.7:23: In this manner he made the ten stands: one casting, one measure, and one form for them all.
verses.7:24: Then he made ten lavers of bronze: each laver held forty baths, each laver was four cubits, and upon each of the ten stands was one laver.
verses.7:25: And he placed five of the stands on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house; and he set the Sea on the right side of the house, toward the east, facing south.
verses.7:26: Hiram also made the lavers, the shovels, and the bowls. So Hiram finished all the work that he performed for King Solomon for the house of the LORD:
verses.7:27: the two pillars, and the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars;
verses.7:28: the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars;
verses.7:29: the ten stands, and the ten lavers upon the stands;
verses.7:30: the one Sea, and the twelve oxen beneath the Sea;
verses.7:31: the pots, the shovels, and the bowls. All these vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of burnished bronze.
verses.7:32: And Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because they were exceedingly numerous; the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
verses.7:33: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
verses.7:34: Thus Solomon made all the furnishings that were in the house of the LORD: the altar of gold, and the table of gold upon which was the showbread;
verses.7:35: the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left before the inner sanctuary, with the blossoms, the lamps, and the tongs of gold;
verses.7:36: the basins, the trimmers, the bowls, the ladles, and the firepans of pure gold; and the hinges of gold, both for the doors of the inner house, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the house, that is, of the temple.
verses.7:37: So all the work that King Solomon performed for the house of the LORD was finished. And Solomon brought in the things that his father David had dedicated: the silver, the gold, and the vessels he placed in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
verses.7:38: Now Solomon was thirteen years in building his own house, and he finished all his house.
verses.7:39: He also built the House of the Forest of Lebanon: its length was one hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams resting upon the pillars.
verses.7:40: And it was paneled with cedar above, over the chambers that were upon the pillars, forty-five in number, fifteen to a row.
verses.7:41: There were window frames in three rows, and window faced window in three tiers.
verses.7:42: All the doorways and doorposts had square frames, and window stood opposite window in three tiers.
verses.7:43: He also made the Hall of Pillars: its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits; and a porch was in front of them, with pillars and a canopy before them.
verses.7:44: And he made the Hall of the Throne, where he would administer judgment, the Hall of Judgment; and it was paneled with cedar from floor to floor.
verses.7:45: And his house where he was to dwell, in the other court inward from the hall, was of like workmanship. He also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom Solomon had taken in marriage.
verses.7:46: All these were made of costly stones, hewn to measure, sawed with saws within and without, from the foundation to the coping, and on the outside as far as the great court.
verses.7:47: The foundation was of costly stones, great stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
verses.7:48: And above were costly stones, hewn to measure, and cedar.
verses.7:49: And the great court all around had three courses of hewn stone and one course of cedar beams, as did the inner court of the house of the LORD and the porch of the house.
verses.8:1: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the chiefs of the fathers' houses of the children of Israel, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, which is Zion.
verses.8:2: And all the men of Israel gathered together to King Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
verses.8:3: So all the elders of Israel came, and the priests lifted up the ark.
verses.8:4: And they brought up the ark of the LORD, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; these the priests and the Levites brought up.
verses.8:5: And King Solomon, and all the congregation of Israel who had assembled to him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen that could neither be counted nor numbered for multitude.
verses.8:6: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.8:7: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.
verses.8:8: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles could be seen from the holy place in front of the inner sanctuary, yet they could not be seen outside; and they remain there to this day.
verses.8:9: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone which Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.
verses.8:10: And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD,
verses.8:11: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.
verses.8:14: Then the king turned his face around and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel was standing.
verses.8:15: And he said, "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to my father David, and with His hand has fulfilled it, saying,
verses.8:16: 'Since the day that I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any of the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that My name might be there; yet I chose David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.8:17: Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.
verses.8:18: But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that it was in your heart.
verses.8:19: Nevertheless, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall come forth from your loins, he shall build the house for My name.'
verses.8:20: So the LORD has established His word which He spoke; and I have risen in the place of my father David and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.
verses.8:21: And there I have appointed a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt."
verses.8:22: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven.
verses.8:23: And he said, "O LORD God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth beneath, who keep covenant and lovingkindness with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart;
verses.8:24: You who have kept with Your servant David my father what You promised him; indeed, You spoke with Your mouth and have fulfilled it with Your hand, as it is this day.
verses.8:25: Therefore now, O LORD God of Israel, keep with Your servant David my father what You spoke to him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man before Me to sit on the throne of Israel, only if your sons take heed to their way, to walk before Me as you have walked before Me.'
verses.8:26: And now, O God of Israel, let Your word, I pray, be confirmed, which You have spoken to Your servant David my father.
verses.8:27: But will God indeed dwell upon the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You; how much less this house which I have built!
verses.8:28: Yet have regard to the prayer of Your servant and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which Your servant is praying before You this day,
verses.8:29: that Your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which You said, 'My name shall be there,' that You may hear the prayer which Your servant prays toward this place.
verses.8:30: And listen to the supplication of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place; hear from Your dwelling place in heaven, and when You hear, forgive.
verses.8:31: When a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and the oath comes before Your altar in this house,
verses.8:32: then hear in heaven, and act, and judge Your servants, condemning the wicked by bringing his way upon his own head, and justifying the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.
verses.8:33: When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, and pray and make supplication to You in this house,
verses.8:34: then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land which You gave to their fathers.
verses.8:35: When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and turn from their sin when You afflict them,
verses.8:36: then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your servants and of Your people Israel, that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk; and give rain upon Your land which You have given to Your people as an inheritance.
verses.8:37: If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence, if there is blight or mildew, locust or caterpillar, if their enemy besieges them in the land of their gates, whatever plague or whatever sickness there is,
verses.8:38: whatever prayer, whatever supplication is made by any man, or by all Your people Israel, when each one knows the plague of his own heart and spreads out his hands toward this house,
verses.8:39: then hear in heaven Your dwelling place, and forgive, and act, and render to every man according to all his ways, whose heart You know—for You alone know the hearts of all the sons of men—
verses.8:40: that they may fear You all the days that they live upon the face of the land which You gave to our fathers.
verses.8:41: Moreover, concerning the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel, when he comes from a far country for the sake of Your name—
verses.8:42: for they shall hear of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this house,
verses.8:43: hear in heaven Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You, that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and that they may know that Your name is called upon this house which I have built.
verses.8:44: When Your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way You send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city which You have chosen and toward the house which I have built for Your name,
verses.8:45: then hear in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.
verses.8:46: When they sin against You—for there is no man who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them before an enemy, so that their captors carry them away captive to the land of the enemy, far or near,
verses.8:47: yet if they take it to heart in the land where they have been carried captive, and repent and make supplication to You in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and committed iniquity; we have acted wickedly,'
verses.8:48: and if they return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies who carried them away captive, and pray to You toward their land which You gave to their fathers, toward the city which You have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for Your name,
verses.8:49: then hear in heaven Your dwelling place their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause,
verses.8:50: and forgive Your people who have sinned against You, and all their transgressions by which they have transgressed against You, and grant them compassion before their captors, that they may have compassion on them;
verses.8:51: for they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace,
verses.8:52: that Your eyes may be open to the supplication of Your servant and to the supplication of Your people Israel, to listen to them whenever they call to You."
verses.8:53: Then Solomon said, "The LORD said that He would dwell in the thick darkness. I have surely built You an exalted house, a settled place for You to abide forever. For You separated them for Yourself as an inheritance from among all the peoples of the earth, as You spoke by the hand of Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord GOD."
verses.8:54: And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and supplication to the LORD, that he arose from before the altar of the LORD, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven.
verses.8:55: Then he stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
verses.8:56: "Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel, according to all that He promised; not one word has failed of all His good promise which He spoke by the hand of His servant Moses.
verses.8:57: May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; may He neither leave us nor forsake us,
verses.8:58: that He may incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments and His statutes and His judgments which He commanded our fathers.
verses.8:59: And may these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, that He may maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires,
verses.8:60: that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God; there is no other.
verses.8:61: Let your heart therefore be wholly devoted to the LORD our God, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments, as at this day."
verses.8:62: Then the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the LORD.
verses.8:63: And Solomon offered as the sacrifice of peace offerings, which he sacrificed to the LORD, twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.
verses.8:64: On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat of the peace offerings.
verses.8:65: And at that time Solomon held the feast, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven more days—fourteen days.
verses.8:66: On the eighth day he sent the people away; and they blessed the king, and went to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
verses.9:1: Now it came to pass, when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the house of the king, and all the desire of Solomon that he was pleased to accomplish,
verses.9:2: that the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, just as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.
verses.9:3: And the LORD said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you have pleaded before Me; I have consecrated this house which you have built, to place My name there forever, and My eyes and My heart shall be there all the days.
verses.9:4: And as for you, if you walk before Me as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and My judgments,
verses.9:5: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, just as I spoke concerning David your father, saying, 'A man shall not be cut off for you from the throne of Israel.'
verses.9:6: But if you and your sons surely turn away from following Me, and do not keep My commandments and My statutes that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
verses.9:7: then I will cut off Israel from the face of the land that I have given to them, and the house that I have consecrated for My name I will cast away from before My face; and Israel shall become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.
verses.9:8: And though this house shall be exalted, everyone who passes by it shall be appalled and shall hiss; and they shall say, 'Why has the LORD done thus to this land and to this house?'
verses.9:9: Then they shall answer, 'Because they forsook the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods, and bowed down to them and served them; therefore the LORD has brought upon them all this calamity.'" However, Pharaoh's daughter went up from the City of David to her house that he had built for her; then he built the Millo.
verses.9:10: Now it came to pass at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the LORD and the house of the king—
verses.9:11: Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber and gold, according to all his desire—that King Solomon then gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
verses.9:12: Then Hiram went out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they were not pleasing in his eyes.
verses.9:13: So he said, "What cities are these that you have given me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul, to this day.
verses.9:14: And Hiram sent to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
verses.9:26: And King Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-Geber, which is beside Eloth on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
verses.9:27: And Hiram sent his servants with the fleet, seamen who knew the sea, together with the servants of Solomon.
verses.9:28: And they went to Ophir and took from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.
verses.10:1: Now the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, and she came to test him with riddles.
verses.10:2: She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels bearing spices, a very great abundance of gold, and precious stones; and when she came to Solomon, she spoke with him of all that was in her heart.
verses.10:3: And Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from the king that he did not explain to her.
verses.10:4: And when the queen of Sheba beheld all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,
verses.10:5: the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their apparel, his cupbearers, and his burnt offering that he offered at the house of the LORD, there was no more spirit in her.
verses.10:6: Then she said to the king, "The report was true that I heard in my own land concerning your words and your wisdom.
verses.10:7: Yet I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes saw it; and behold, the half was not told to me! You have exceeded in wisdom and prosperity the report that I heard.
verses.10:8: Blessed are your men, blessed are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
verses.10:9: Blessed be the LORD your God, who delighted in you to set you upon the throne of Israel! Because the LORD loves Israel forever, therefore He has made you king, to execute justice and righteousness."
verses.10:10: Then she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as that which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.10:11: Moreover, the fleet of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought from Ophir a very great quantity of almug wood and precious stones.
verses.10:12: And from the almug wood the king made supports for the house of the LORD and for the house of the king, as well as harps and stringed instruments for the singers. No such almug wood has come, nor has it been seen, to this day.
verses.10:13: And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, besides what he gave her according to the royal bounty of King Solomon. Then she turned and went to her own land, she and her servants.
verses.10:14: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.10:15: besides what came from the traveling merchants, and from the traffic of the traders, and from all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land.
verses.10:16: And King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each large shield.
verses.10:17: He also made three hundred shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
verses.10:18: Moreover, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with refined gold.
verses.10:19: The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was rounded at the back; there were armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the armrests.
verses.10:20: And twelve lions stood there on the six steps, on the one side and on the other; nothing like it had been made in any kingdom.
verses.10:21: All the drinking vessels of King Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. None were of silver; it was considered as nothing in the days of Solomon.
verses.10:22: Now this is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon raised to build the house of the LORD, his own house, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer. Solomon built Gezer, Lower Beth-Horon, Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land, as well as all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, the cities for the chariots, the cities for the horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion. All the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of the children of Israel—their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel had not been able to utterly destroy—these Solomon conscripted for forced labor, to this day. But of the children of Israel Solomon made no slaves, because they were men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and commanders of his chariots and his horsemen. For the king had a Tarshish fleet at sea with the fleet of Hiram; once every three years the Tarshish fleet came bringing gold and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
verses.10:23: Thus King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
verses.10:24: And all the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
verses.10:25: And each of them brought his tribute—articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules—at a set rate year by year.
verses.10:26: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen. Solomon also gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.
verses.10:27: And the king made silver in Jerusalem like stones, and he made cedars as abundant as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland.
verses.10:28: And Solomon's import of horses was from Egypt and Kue; the king's merchants obtained them from Kue at a price.
verses.10:29: Now a chariot was brought up and exported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty; and thus, by their means, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Syria.
verses.11:1: Now King Solomon loved many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh—Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women. And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned his heart aside.
verses.11:2: From the nations concerning whom the LORD had said to the children of Israel, "You shall not enter among them, nor shall they enter among you; surely they will turn your heart after their gods"—to these Solomon clung in love.
verses.11:4: And it came to pass, at the time of Solomon's old age, that his wives turned his heart after other gods; and his heart was not wholly devoted to the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
verses.11:5: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, on the mountain facing Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.
verses.11:6: And Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites.
verses.11:7: And he did likewise for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
verses.11:8: Thus Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD, and did not follow the LORD fully, as David his father had done.
verses.11:9: Therefore the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice,
verses.11:10: and had commanded him concerning this matter, that he should not go after other gods; yet he did not keep that which the LORD had commanded.
verses.11:11: So the LORD said to Solomon, "Because this has been found in you, and you have not kept My covenant and My statutes which I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
verses.11:12: Nevertheless, I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
verses.11:13: However, I will not tear away the entire kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David, and for the sake of Jerusalem which I have chosen."
verses.11:14: Now the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; he was of the royal seed in Edom. And God also raised up an adversary against him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer, king of Zobah. He gathered men to himself and became captain of a marauding band when David slew them; and they went to Damascus and dwelt in it, and reigned in Damascus.
verses.11:15: For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, that he struck down every male in Edom.
verses.11:16: For Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
verses.11:17: But Hadad fled, he and certain Edomite men of his father's servants with him, to go into Egypt, while Hadad was still a little boy.
verses.11:18: Then they arose from Midian and came to Paran; and they took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, appointed provisions for him, and granted him land.
verses.11:19: And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
verses.11:20: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him his son Genubath, whom Tahpenes weaned within the house of Pharaoh; and Genubath dwelt in Pharaoh's household among the sons of Pharaoh.
verses.11:21: Now when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Send me away, that I may go to my own land."
verses.11:22: Then Pharaoh said to him, "What have you lacked with me, that behold, you seek to go to your own land?" And he answered, "Nothing; nevertheless, surely send me away."
verses.11:25: He was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, in addition to the harm that Hadad wrought; and he abhorred Israel and reigned over Aram.
verses.11:26: Also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, Solomon's servant—whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow—lifted up his hand against the king.
verses.11:27: And this was the occasion on which he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach in the City of David his father.
verses.11:28: Now the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor; and Solomon observed that the young man was diligent in his work, so he appointed him over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
verses.11:29: And it came to pass at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road; and he was wearing a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the open field.
verses.11:30: Then Ahijah took hold of the new garment that was on him, and tore it into twelve pieces.
verses.11:31: And he said to Jeroboam, "Take for yourself ten pieces; for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Behold, I am tearing the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give the ten tribes to you,
verses.11:32: though he shall have the one tribe for the sake of My servant David, and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel,
verses.11:33: because they have forsaken Me, and bowed down to Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, to Chemosh the god of Moab, and to Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in My ways to do what is right in My sight, and to keep My statutes and My judgments, as David his father did.
verses.11:34: However, I will not take the entire kingdom out of his hand, for I will make him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of My servant David whom I chose, who kept My commandments and My statutes.
verses.11:35: But I will take the kingdom out of the hand of his son and give it to you—the ten tribes.
verses.11:36: And to his son I will give one tribe, so that My servant David may always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for Myself, to place My name there.
verses.11:37: So I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.
verses.11:38: And it shall be, if you heed all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight, to keep My statutes and My commandments, as My servant David did, then I will be with you and build for you a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to you.'"
verses.11:40: Therefore Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death; but Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and remained in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
verses.11:41: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
verses.11:42: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
verses.11:43: Then Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David his father, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place. And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it—for he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon—that Jeroboam remained in Egypt.
verses.12:1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
verses.12:3: Then they sent and summoned him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.12:4: "Your father made our yoke harsh; now therefore lighten the harsh servitude of your father and his heavy yoke which he laid upon us, and we will serve you."
verses.12:5: And he said to them, "Go away for three days more, then return to me." So the people went away.
verses.12:6: Then King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before his father Solomon while he was still alive, saying, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
verses.12:7: They spoke to him, saying, "If today you become a servant to this people, serving them, answering them, and speaking good words to them, then they will be your servants all the days."
verses.12:8: But he forsook the counsel of the elders which they had given him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
verses.12:9: And he said to them, "What do you advise that we should answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke which your father laid upon us'?"
verses.12:10: Then the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, "Thus you shall speak to this people who have spoken to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us'—thus you shall say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins!
verses.12:11: And now, whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.'"
verses.12:12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.12:13: Then the king answered the people harshly, and forsook the counsel of the elders which they had given him;
verses.12:14: and he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions."
verses.12:15: So the king did not listen to the people; for the turn of events was from the LORD, that He might establish His word, which the LORD had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.12:16: Now when all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, saying, "What portion do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, O Israel! Now look to your own house, O David!" So Israel departed to their tents.
verses.12:18: Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor; and all Israel stoned him with stones, so that he died. Therefore King Rehoboam hastily mounted his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
verses.12:20: And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent and called him to the congregation, and made him king over all Israel. None followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.12:21: Now when Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—one hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel, to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
verses.12:22: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
verses.12:23: "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, saying,
verses.12:24: 'Thus says the LORD: You shall not go up nor fight against your brethren, the children of Israel. Let every man return to his house, for this matter is from Me.'" Therefore they obeyed the word of the LORD, and turned back to go according to the word of the LORD. At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick. And Jeroboam said to his wife, "Please arise and disguise yourself, so that they may not know that you are the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. Behold, Ahijah the prophet is there, who spoke concerning me that I should be king over this people. And take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him; he will tell you what will become of the child." And Jeroboam's wife did so; she arose and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were set because of his old age. And the LORD had said to Ahijah, "Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to inquire of you concerning her son, for he is sick; thus and thus you shall speak to her, for it will be, when she comes in, that she will pretend to be another woman." And it came to pass, when Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps as she came through the doorway, that he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why do you pretend to be another? For I have been sent to you with harsh tidings. Therefore, behold, I will bring calamity upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both bond and free in Israel; and I will sweep away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam as a man sweeps away refuse until it is all gone. The dogs shall eat whoever belongs to Jeroboam and dies in the city, and the birds of the air shall eat whoever dies in the field; for the LORD has spoken. Arise therefore, go to your own house. When your feet enter the city, the child shall die. And all Israel shall mourn for him and bury him, for he is the only one of Jeroboam who shall come to the grave, because in him there is found some good thing toward the LORD, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam." Then Jeroboam's wife arose and departed, and came to Tirzah. As she came to the threshold of the house, the child died. And they buried him and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke by the hand of His servant Ahijah the prophet.
verses.12:25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and dwelt there; and he went out from there and built Penuel.
verses.12:26: And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Now the kingdom may return to the house of David.
verses.12:27: If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will turn back to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."
verses.12:28: Therefore the king took counsel and made two calves of gold, and said to them, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Behold your gods, O Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt!"
verses.12:29: And he set up one in Bethel, and the other he placed in Dan.
verses.12:30: Now this thing became a sin, for the people went before the one as far as Dan.
verses.12:31: He also made shrines on the high places, and appointed priests from every rank of the people, who were not of the sons of Levi.
verses.12:32: And Jeroboam instituted a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that was in Judah, and he went up to the altar. So he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made; and at Bethel he installed the priests of the high places which he had made.
verses.12:33: Thus he went up to the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in the month which he had devised from his own heart; and he ordained a feast for the children of Israel, and went up to the altar to burn incense.
verses.13:1: And behold, a man of God came from Judah by the word of the LORD to Bethel, while Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.
verses.13:2: And he cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD, and said, "O altar, altar! Thus says the LORD: 'Behold, a son shall be born to the house of David—Josiah is his name—and upon you he shall sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you, and men shall burn human bones upon you.'"
verses.13:3: And he gave a sign that same day, saying, "This is the sign which the LORD has spoken: Behold, the altar shall be split apart, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out."
verses.13:4: Now it came to pass when the king heard the word of the man of God, which he cried out against the altar in Bethel, that Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him!" Then his hand, which he had stretched out toward him, withered, so that he was not able to draw it back to himself.
verses.13:5: The altar also was split apart, and the ashes were poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
verses.13:6: Then the king answered and said to the man of God, "Please implore the favor of the LORD your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me." So the man of God implored the favor of the LORD, and the king's hand was restored to him, and became as it was before.
verses.13:7: And the king spoke to the man of God, "Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward."
verses.13:8: But the man of God said to the king, "If you were to give me half of your house, I would not go in with you; nor would I eat bread nor drink water in this place.
