verses.13:9: For so I was commanded by the word of the LORD, saying, 'You shall not eat bread, nor drink water, nor return by the way you came.'"
verses.13:10: So he went by another way, and did not return by the way by which he had come to Bethel.
verses.13:11: Now a certain old prophet dwelt in Bethel, and his son came and told him all the work that the man of God had done that day in Bethel; the words also which he had spoken to the king, these they told to their father.
verses.13:12: And their father spoke to them, "Which way did he go?" Now his sons had seen the way that the man of God who came from Judah had gone.
verses.13:13: So he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it.
verses.13:14: And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under the terebinth tree. Then he said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" And he said, "I am."
verses.13:15: Then he said to him, "Come home with me and eat bread."
verses.13:16: And he said, "I cannot return with you nor go in with you; neither will I eat bread nor drink water with you in this place.
verses.13:17: For a word came to me by the word of the LORD: 'You shall not eat bread nor drink water there, nor turn back to go by the way by which you came.'"
verses.13:18: Then he said to him, "I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, 'Bring him back with you to your house, that he may eat bread and drink water.'" He lied to him.
verses.13:19: So he went back with him, and ate bread in his house, and drank water.
verses.13:20: Now it came to pass, as they were sitting at the table, that the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back;
verses.13:21: and he cried out to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, "Thus says the LORD: Because you have rebelled against the word of the LORD, and have not kept the commandment which the LORD your God commanded you,
verses.13:22: but came back and ate bread and drank water in the place of which He spoke to you, 'Do not eat bread and do not drink water,' your corpse shall not come to the tomb of your fathers."
verses.13:23: So it came to pass, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
verses.13:24: And when he departed, a lion met him on the road and slew him. And his corpse was cast on the road, and the donkey was standing beside it; the lion also was standing beside the corpse.
verses.13:25: And behold, men passed by and saw the corpse cast on the road, and the lion standing beside the corpse. And they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.
verses.13:26: Now when the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard it, he said, "It is the man of God who rebelled against the word of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered him to the lion, which has torn him and slain him, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke to him."
verses.13:28: Then he went and found his corpse cast on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse. The lion had not eaten the corpse nor torn the donkey.
verses.13:29: And the prophet took up the corpse of the man of God, laid it upon the donkey, and brought it back; and he came to the city of the old prophet to mourn and to bury him.
verses.13:30: Then he laid his corpse in his own tomb; and they lamented over him, saying, "Alas, my brother!"
verses.13:31: And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, "When I die, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
verses.13:32: For the word which he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the shrines of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass."
verses.13:33: After this event Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but again he made priests of the high places from every class of the people; whoever wished, he consecrated, that he might become one of the priests of the high places.
verses.13:34: And this thing became sin to the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off and to destroy it from the face of the earth.
verses.14:21: Now Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put His name there. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
verses.14:22: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they provoked Him to jealousy more than all that their fathers had done, with their sins which they committed.
verses.14:23: For they also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
verses.14:24: And there were also male cult prostitutes in the land. They acted according to all the abominations of the nations which the LORD had cast out before the children of Israel.
verses.14:25: Now it came to pass in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
verses.14:26: And he took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took away everything. He also took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
verses.14:27: Then King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard, who guarded the doorway of the king's house.
verses.14:28: And it was so, whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, that the guards would bear them, and then bring them back into the guardroom.
verses.14:29: Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:30: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
verses.14:31: So Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. Then Abijam his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: Now in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.
verses.15:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
verses.15:3: And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had committed before him; and his heart was not wholly devoted to the LORD his God, as was the heart of his father David.
verses.15:4: Nevertheless, for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, by raising up his son after him and by establishing Jerusalem,
verses.15:5: because David did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and did not turn aside from all that He commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
verses.15:7: Now the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
verses.15:8: And Abijam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:9: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa began to reign as king of Judah.
verses.15:10: He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
verses.15:11: And Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as David his father had done.
verses.15:12: He banished the male cult prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
verses.15:13: Moreover, he removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made a repulsive image for Asherah; and Asa cut down her repulsive image and burned it at the Brook Kidron.
verses.15:14: Yet the high places were not removed; nevertheless the heart of Asa was wholly devoted to the LORD all his days.
verses.15:15: And he brought the dedicated things of his father and the dedicated things of the house of the LORD—silver and gold and vessels.
verses.15:16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
verses.15:17: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, that he might allow no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.15:18: Then Asa took all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the treasuries of the king's house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants; and King Asa sent them to Ben-Hadad the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,
verses.15:19: "Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you a present of silver and gold; go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, that he may withdraw from me."
verses.15:20: So Ben-Hadad heeded King Asa, and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel; and he struck Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and all Chinneroth, together with all the land of Naphtali.
verses.15:21: Now when Baasha heard of it, he ceased building Ramah and remained in Tirzah.
verses.15:22: Then King Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah—none was exempt—and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had built; and with them King Asa built Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.
verses.15:23: Now the rest of all the acts of Asa, all his might, all that he did, and the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Yet in the time of his old age he became diseased in his feet.
verses.15:24: So Asa slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:25: Now Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
verses.15:26: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the way of his father and in his sin by which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:27: Then Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were laying siege to Gibbethon.
verses.15:28: Thus Baasha put him to death in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:29: And it came to pass, as soon as he became king, that he struck down all the house of Jeroboam; he did not leave to Jeroboam anyone who breathed, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke by the hand of His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
verses.15:30: because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he had sinned and by which he had caused Israel to sin, through his provocation by which he provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger.
verses.15:31: Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:33: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah began to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned twenty-four years.
verses.15:34: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin by which he had caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:1: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
verses.16:2: "Because I lifted you up out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, yet you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused My people Israel to sin, to provoke Me to anger with their sins,
verses.16:3: behold, I will utterly sweep away Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.16:4: Whoever belongs to Baasha and dies in the city the dogs shall eat, and whoever belongs to him and dies in the field the birds of the heavens shall eat."
verses.16:5: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:6: So Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his place.
verses.16:7: Moreover, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Jehu the son of Hanani the prophet against Baasha and against his house, because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands, in becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and also because he had struck it down.
verses.16:8: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha began to reign over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned two years.
verses.16:9: Now his servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him while he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.
verses.16:10: And Zimri went in and struck him down and put him to death in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
verses.16:11: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat upon his throne, that he struck down all the house of Baasha; he did not leave him a single male, neither of his kinsmen nor of his friends.
verses.16:12: Thus Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke against Baasha by the hand of Jehu the prophet,
verses.16:13: for all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, which they had sinned and by which they had caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vain idols.
verses.16:14: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:15: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah; now the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
verses.16:16: And the people who were encamped heard it said, "Zimri has conspired and has also struck down the king." Therefore all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp.
verses.16:17: Then Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirzah.
verses.16:18: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he entered the citadel of the king's house and burned the king's house down over himself with fire, and died,
verses.16:19: because of his sins which he had sinned in doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, in walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he committed in causing Israel to sin.
verses.16:20: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy that he made, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:21: Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath to make him king, and the other half followed Omri.
verses.16:22: But the people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni the son of Ginath; so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
verses.16:23: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri began to reign over Israel, and he reigned twelve years; six years he reigned in Tirzah.
verses.16:24: And he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built upon the hill, and called the name of the city that he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill.
verses.16:25: And Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
verses.16:26: For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin by which he had caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vain idols.
verses.16:27: Now the rest of the acts of Omri that he did, and the might that he displayed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:28: So Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his place. And the remnant of the male cult prostitutes, who remained in the days of his father Asa, he purged from the land. Now there was no king in Edom; a deputy was king. Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but he did not go, for the ships were wrecked at Ezion Geber. Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." But Jehoshaphat was not willing.
verses.16:29: Now Ahab the son of Omri began to reign over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah; and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
verses.16:30: And Ahab the son of Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
verses.16:31: And it came to pass, as though it were a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took as his wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians; and he went and served Baal and worshiped him.
verses.16:32: And he erected an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
verses.16:33: And Ahab made an Asherah; and Ahab did more to provoke the LORD God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.16:34: In his days Hiel of Bethel built Jericho; at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest son he set up its gates, according to the word of the LORD, which He spoke by the hand of Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.17:1: And Elijah the Tishbite, of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the LORD God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except according to my word."
verses.17:2: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.17:3: "Depart from here and turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Brook Cherith, which lies before the Jordan.
verses.17:4: And it shall be that you shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to sustain you there."
verses.17:5: So he went and acted according to the word of the LORD, for he went and dwelt by the Brook Cherith, which lies before the Jordan.
verses.17:6: And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.
verses.17:7: And it came to pass after a span of days that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
verses.17:8: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.17:9: "Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. Behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain you."
verses.17:10: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the entrance of the city, behold, a widow woman was there gathering sticks. And he called to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a vessel, that I may drink."
verses.17:11: And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her and said, "Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand."
verses.17:12: Then she said, "As the LORD your God lives, I do not have a baked loaf, only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the flask; and behold, I am gathering a couple of sticks that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die."
verses.17:13: And Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid; go and do according to your word, only make me a small cake from it first and bring it out to me, and afterward prepare some for yourself and your son.
verses.17:14: For thus says the LORD God of Israel: 'The jar of flour shall not be spent, nor shall the flask of oil fail, until the day the LORD gives rain upon the face of the ground.'"
verses.17:15: So she went and acted according to the word of Elijah; and she and he and her household ate for many days.
verses.17:16: The jar of flour was not spent, nor did the flask of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke by the hand of Elijah.
verses.17:17: Now it came to pass after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick. And his sickness was exceedingly severe, until no breath remained in him.
verses.17:18: So she said to Elijah, "What have I to do with you, O man of God? Have you come to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance, and to put my son to death?"
verses.17:19: And he said to her, "Give me your son." So he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper chamber where he was staying, and laid him upon his own bed.
verses.17:20: Then he cried out to the LORD and said, "O LORD my God, have You also brought calamity upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by putting her son to death?"
verses.17:21: And he stretched himself out over the child three times, and cried out to the LORD and said, "O LORD my God, I pray, let the soul of this child return into him."
verses.17:22: Then the LORD hearkened to the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child returned into him, and he revived.
verses.17:23: And Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper chamber into the house, and gave him to his mother. And Elijah said, "See, your son lives!"
verses.17:24: Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now by this I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth."
verses.18:1: And it came to pass after many days that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go, present yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain upon the face of the ground."
verses.18:2: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab; and the famine was severe in Samaria.
verses.18:3: And Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was over the household. Now Obadiah feared the LORD exceedingly.
verses.18:4: For it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD, that Obadiah took one hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men to a cave, and sustained them with bread and water.
verses.18:5: And Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the brooks; perhaps we may find grass and keep the horses and mules alive, so that we do not have to cut off any of the beasts."
verses.18:6: So they divided the land between them to pass through it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
verses.18:7: Now as Obadiah was on the way, behold, Elijah met him. And he recognized him, and fell upon his face, and said, "Is this indeed you, my lord Elijah?"
verses.18:8: And he said to him, "It is I. Go, tell your lord, 'Behold, Elijah is here.'"
verses.18:9: Then he said, "How have I sinned, that you are delivering your servant into the hand of Ahab, to put me to death?
verses.18:10: As the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you; and when they said, 'He is not here,' he made the kingdom and the nation swear an oath that they could not find you.
verses.18:11: And now you say, 'Go, tell your lord: Behold, Elijah is here.'
verses.18:12: And it shall come to pass, as soon as I depart from you, that the Spirit of the LORD will carry you to a place I do not know; and when I come to tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will slay me. Yet your servant has feared the LORD from my youth.
verses.18:13: Was it not told to my lord what I did when Jezebel slew the prophets of the LORD, how I hid one hundred men of the prophets of the LORD, by fifties in a cave, and sustained them with bread and water?
verses.18:14: And now you say, 'Go, tell your lord: Behold, Elijah is here,' and he will slay me!"
verses.18:15: Then Elijah said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely present myself to him today."
verses.18:16: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him; and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
verses.18:17: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said to him, "Is this indeed you, O troubler of Israel?"
verses.18:18: And he answered, "I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father's house have, in that you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and you have gone after the Baals.
verses.18:19: Now therefore, send and gather all Israel to me on Mount Carmel, and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal, and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel's table."
verses.18:20: So Ahab sent throughout all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together on Mount Carmel.
verses.18:21: And Elijah drew near to all the people and said, "How long will you limp between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him." Yet the people did not answer him a word.
verses.18:22: Then Elijah said to the people, "I alone remain a prophet of the LORD, whereas Baal's prophets are four hundred and fifty men.
verses.18:23: Therefore let them give us two bulls, and let them choose one bull for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it upon the wood, yet put no fire under it; and I will prepare the other bull, and lay it upon the wood, yet put no fire under it.
verses.18:24: Then call upon the name of your god, and I will call upon the name of the LORD; and the God who answers by fire, He is God." So all the people answered and said, "The word is good."
verses.18:25: Now Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are many; and call upon the name of your god, yet put no fire under it."
verses.18:26: So they took the bull which had been given to them and prepared it, and called upon the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, "O Baal, answer us!" Yet there was no voice, and no one answered. And they limped about the altar which had been made.
verses.18:27: And it came to pass at noon that Elijah mocked them and said, "Cry aloud, for he is a god; either he is meditating, or he has turned aside, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened."
verses.18:28: So they cried aloud, and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and lances, until the blood gushed out upon them.
verses.18:29: And when midday had passed, they prophesied until the time of the evening offering; yet there was no voice, no one answered, and no one paid heed.
verses.18:30: Then Elijah said to all the people, "Draw near to me." So all the people drew near to him. And he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.
verses.18:31: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come, saying, "Israel shall be your name."
verses.18:32: Then with the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD; and he made a trench around the altar, large enough to hold two seahs of seed.
verses.18:33: And he arranged the wood, and cut the bull in pieces, and laid it upon the wood.
verses.18:34: And he said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it upon the burnt offering and upon the wood." Then he said, "Do it a second time," and they did it a second time; and he said, "Do it a third time," and they did it a third time.
verses.18:35: So the water ran all around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.
verses.18:36: And it came to pass, at the time of the evening offering, that Elijah the prophet drew near and said, "O LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that You are God in Israel and that I am Your servant, and that I have done all these things at Your word.
verses.18:37: Answer me, O LORD, answer me, that this people may know that You, O LORD, are God, and that You have turned their hearts back again."
verses.18:38: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water that was in the trench.
verses.18:39: Now when all the people saw it, they fell upon their faces; and they said, "The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!"
verses.18:40: And Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal! Do not let one of them escape!" So they seized them; and Elijah brought them down to the Brook Kishon and slew them there.
verses.18:41: Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of the rushing of rain."
verses.18:42: So Ahab went up to eat and drink. And Elijah went up to the summit of Carmel; then he bowed down to the ground and placed his face between his knees.
verses.18:43: And he said to his servant, "Go up now, look toward the sea." So he went up and looked, and said, "There is nothing." And he said, "Go back seven times."
verses.18:44: And it came to pass at the seventh time that he said, "Behold, a small cloud, like a man's hand, is rising out of the sea!" Then he said, "Go up, say to Ahab, 'Harness your chariot and go down, lest the rain detain you.'"
verses.18:45: And it came to pass in a little while that the heavens grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain. So Ahab rode away and went to Jezreel.
verses.18:46: Then the hand of the LORD was upon Elijah; and he girded up his loins and ran ahead of Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
verses.19:1: And Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done, and all about how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.
verses.19:2: Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "May the gods do so, and more also; by this time tomorrow I will surely make your life like the life of one of them."
verses.19:3: And when he saw this, he arose and went for his life, and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.
verses.19:4: But he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a broom tree. And he requested for himself that he might die, and said, "It is enough! Now, O LORD, take my life, for I am no better than my fathers."
verses.19:5: Then he lay down and slept under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat."
verses.19:6: And he looked, and behold, near his head was a cake baked on hot stones and a jar of water. So he ate and drank, and lay down again.
verses.19:7: And the angel of the LORD returned a second time, and touched him, and said, "Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you."
verses.19:8: So he arose, and ate and drank; and he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights, to Horeb, the mountain of God.
verses.19:9: And there he entered into the cave and spent the night there; and behold, the word of the LORD came to him, and He said to him, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
verses.19:10: And he said, "I have been exceedingly zealous for the LORD God of hosts; for the children of Israel have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and slain Your prophets with the sword. And I, even I alone, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away."
verses.19:11: Then He said, "Go forth, and stand upon the mountain before the LORD." And behold, the LORD was passing by, and a great and mighty wind tore apart the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD; yet the LORD was not in the wind. And after the wind came an earthquake, yet the LORD was not in the earthquake.
verses.19:12: And after the earthquake came a fire, yet the LORD was not in the fire; and after the fire, the sound of a gentle stillness.
verses.19:13: And it came to pass, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And behold, a voice came to him and said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
verses.19:14: And he said, "I have been exceedingly zealous for the LORD God of hosts; for the children of Israel have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and slain Your prophets with the sword. And I, even I alone, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away."
verses.19:15: Then the LORD said to him, "Go, return on your way toward the wilderness of Damascus; and when you arrive, you shall anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
verses.19:16: Also you shall anoint Jehu the son of Nimshi as king over Israel. And Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel Meholah you shall anoint as prophet in your place.
verses.19:17: And it shall come to pass, that whoever escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu shall put to death; and whoever escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha shall put to death.
verses.19:18: Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him."
verses.19:19: So he departed from there and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he was with the twelfth. Then Elijah passed over to him and cast his mantle upon him.
verses.19:20: And he left the oxen and ran after Elijah, and said, "Please let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you." And he said to him, "Go, return; for what have I done to you?"
verses.19:21: So he turned back from following him, and took the yoke of oxen and slaughtered them, and boiled their flesh using the equipment of the oxen, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he arose and followed Elijah, and ministered to him.
verses.20:1: And it came to pass after these things that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard which was in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.20:2: So Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard, that it may be mine for a vegetable garden, because it is near, beside my house; and I will give you a better vineyard than it in its place. If it is good in your eyes, I will give you its price in silver."
verses.20:3: But Naboth said to Ahab, "Far be it from me, by the LORD, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!"
verses.20:4: So Ahab came into his house sullen and vexed because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him; for he had said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." And he lay down on his bed, and turned away his face, and did not eat bread.
verses.20:5: Then Jezebel his wife came to him and spoke to him, "Why is your spirit so sullen, and why are you not eating bread?"
verses.20:6: And he spoke to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for silver, or if you prefer, I will give you a vineyard in its place.' Yet he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
verses.20:7: Then Jezebel his wife said to him, "Do you now exercise kingship over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and let your heart be glad; I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
verses.20:8: So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent letters to the elders and to the nobles who were in his city, dwelling with Naboth.
verses.20:9: And she wrote in the letters, saying, "Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people;
verses.20:10: and seat two men, sons of Belial, opposite him, and let them bear witness against him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then bring him out and stone him, that he may die."
verses.20:11: So the men of his city, the elders and the nobles who dwelt in his city, did as Jezebel had sent word to them, just as it was written in the letters which she had sent to them.
verses.20:12: They proclaimed a fast, and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.20:13: And the two men, sons of Belial, came in and sat opposite him; and the men of Belial bore witness against him, against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, "Naboth has cursed God and the king!" Then they brought him outside the city and stoned him with stones, so that he died.
verses.20:14: Then they sent word to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."
verses.20:15: And it came to pass, when Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, that Jezebel said to Ahab, "Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver; for Naboth is not alive, but dead."
verses.20:16: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab arose to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
verses.20:17: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.20:18: "Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.
verses.20:19: And you shall speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: Have you murdered and also taken possession?' And you shall speak to him, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: In the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, the dogs shall lick your blood, even yours.'"
verses.20:20: And Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, O my enemy?" And he answered, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.20:21: Behold, I will bring calamity upon you; I will sweep away those who come after you, and will cut off from Ahab every male, both bond and free, in Israel;
verses.20:22: and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked wrath, and have caused Israel to sin.
verses.20:23: And concerning Jezebel also the LORD has spoken, saying, 'The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.'
verses.20:24: Whoever belongs to Ahab and dies in the city, the dogs shall eat; and whoever dies in the field, the birds of the heavens shall eat."
verses.20:25: Surely there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the sight of the LORD, whom Jezebel his wife incited.
verses.20:26: And he acted very abominably in going after idols, according to all that the Amorites had done, whom the LORD had cast out before the children of Israel.
verses.20:27: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard these words, that he tore his garments, and put sackcloth on his flesh, and fasted, and lay in sackcloth, and walked about quietly.
verses.20:28: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.20:29: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before Me? Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the calamity in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the calamity upon his house."
verses.21:1: Now Ben-Hadad king of Syria assembled all his host, and thirty-two kings were with him, with horses and chariots. And he went up, laid siege to Samaria, and fought against it.
verses.21:2: Then he sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel,
verses.21:3: and said to him, "Thus says Ben-Hadad: 'Your silver and your gold belong to me; your fairest wives and your children also belong to me.'"
verses.21:4: And the king of Israel answered and said, "According to your word, my lord the king, I am yours, and all that is mine."
verses.21:5: Then the messengers came back and said, "Thus speaks Ben-Hadad, saying, 'Indeed I sent to you, saying, "You shall give to me your silver and your gold, your wives and your children,"
verses.21:6: yet about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they shall search your house and the houses of your servants; and it shall come to pass that whatever is delightful to your eyes, they shall place in their hands and carry away.'"
verses.21:7: So the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "Consider now, and see how this man seeks evil; for he sent to me for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I did not withhold them from him."
verses.21:8: And all the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen, nor consent."
verses.21:9: Therefore he said to the messengers of Ben-Hadad, "Say to my lord the king, 'All that you sent for to your servant at the first I will do, but this matter I cannot do.'" And the messengers departed and brought back word to him.
verses.21:10: Then Ben-Hadad sent to him and said, "May the gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people who follow at my feet."
verses.21:11: And the king of Israel answered and said, "Tell him, 'Do not let him who girds on his armor boast like him who takes it off.'"
verses.21:12: And it came to pass, when he heard this word—while he and the kings were drinking in the pavilions—that he said to his servants, "Set yourselves in array!" So they set themselves in array against the city.
verses.21:13: And behold, a certain prophet drew near to Ahab king of Israel and said, "Thus says the LORD: 'Have you seen all this great multitude? Behold, I am giving it into your hand today, and you shall know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.21:14: And Ahab said, "By whom?" And he said, "Thus says the LORD: 'By the young men of the governors of the provinces.'" Then he said, "Who shall begin the battle?" And he answered, "You."
verses.21:15: Then he mustered the young men of the governors of the provinces, and they were two hundred and thirty-two; and after them he mustered all the people, all the children of Israel—seven thousand.
verses.21:16: And they marched out at noon, while Ben-Hadad was drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings, the thirty-two kings who were aiding him.
verses.21:17: The young men of the governors of the provinces went out first. And Ben-Hadad sent out to inquire, and they reported to him, saying, "Men have come out from Samaria."
verses.21:18: So he said, "If they have come out for peace, capture them alive; and if they have come out for war, capture them alive."
verses.21:19: So these went out from the city—the young men of the governors of the provinces, and the army that followed behind them.
verses.21:20: And each one struck down his man; so the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them, and Ben-Hadad king of Syria escaped on a horse with the horsemen.
verses.21:21: Then the king of Israel went out and struck the horses and the chariots, and he struck the Syrians with a great slaughter.
verses.21:22: And the prophet drew near to the king of Israel and said to him, "Go, strengthen yourself; take heed and see what you should do, for at the turn of the year the king of Syria will come up against you."
verses.21:23: Now the servants of the king of Syria said to him, "Their gods are gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we. Yet let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.
verses.21:24: And do this thing: remove the kings, each from his post, and appoint commanders in their place.
verses.21:25: And number for yourself an army like the army that fell from you, horse for horse and chariot for chariot; then let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they." And he heeded their voice and did so.
verses.21:26: So it came to pass at the turn of the year that Ben-Hadad mustered the Syrians and went up to Aphek to wage war against Israel.
verses.21:27: And the children of Israel were mustered and provisioned, and went out to meet them. And the children of Israel encamped opposite them like two little flocks of goats, while the Syrians filled the land.
verses.21:28: Then a man of God drew near and spoke to the king of Israel, saying, "Thus says the LORD: 'Because the Syrians have said, "The LORD is God of the hills, and He is not God of the valleys," therefore I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you shall know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.21:29: And they encamped one opposite the other for seven days. And it came to pass on the seventh day that the battle was joined, and the children of Israel struck down one hundred thousand foot soldiers of the Syrians in one day.
verses.21:30: And the rest fled to Aphek, into the city, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand of the men who remained. And Ben-Hadad fled and came into the city, into an inner chamber.
verses.21:31: Then his servants said to him, "Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Please let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes upon our heads, and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will spare your life."
verses.21:32: So they girded sackcloth around their waists and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" And he said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
verses.21:33: Now the men were watching eagerly for a favorable sign, and they quickly seized upon his word and said, "Your brother Ben-Hadad!" Then he said, "Go, bring him." So Ben-Hadad came out to him, and he brought him up into the chariot.
verses.21:34: And Ben-Hadad said to him, "The cities that my father took from your father I will restore, and you may establish market streets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father established in Samaria." Then Ahab said, "On the basis of this covenant I will let you go." So he made a covenant with him and sent him away.
verses.21:35: Now a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the LORD, "Strike me, please." Yet the man refused to strike him.
verses.21:36: Then he said to him, "Because you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, behold, as soon as you depart from me, a lion shall strike you down." And when he departed from his side, a lion found him and struck him down.
verses.21:37: Then he found another man and said, "Strike me, please." And the man struck him hard and wounded him.
verses.21:38: So the prophet went and waited for the king along the road, having disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.
verses.21:39: And as the king was passing by, he cried out to the king and said, "Your servant went out into the midst of the battle; and behold, a man turned aside and brought a man to me, and said, 'Guard this man; if by any means he goes missing, then your life shall be for his life, or else you shall pay a talent of silver.'
verses.21:40: And while your servant was occupied here and there, he vanished." And the king of Israel said to him, "So shall your judgment be; you yourself have decided it."
verses.21:41: Then he quickly removed the bandage from over his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.
verses.21:42: And he said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I devoted to destruction, therefore your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people.'"
verses.21:43: So the king of Israel went to his house, sullen and vexed, and came to Samaria.
verses.22:1: And they remained three years without war between Syria and Israel.
verses.22:2: And it came to pass in the third year that Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
verses.22:3: And the king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth Gilead is ours, yet we remain still, not taking it out of the hand of the king of Syria?"
verses.22:4: Then he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to war at Ramoth Gilead?" And Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel, "I am as you are, my people are as your people, and my horses are as your horses."
verses.22:5: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Inquire, please, for the word of the LORD today."
verses.22:6: Then the king of Israel assembled the prophets, about four hundred men, and asked them, "Shall I march against Ramoth Gilead for battle, or shall I hold back?" And they replied, "Go up, and the Lord will give it into the king's hand."
verses.22:7: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of him?"
verses.22:8: So the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man by whom to inquire of the LORD, yet I hate him, for he does not prophesy good concerning me, but only evil—Micaiah the son of Imlah." And Jehoshaphat said, "Let the king not say so."
verses.22:9: Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah the son of Imlah quickly."
verses.22:10: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah were sitting each upon his throne, arrayed in their robes, at a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.22:11: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah had made for himself horns of iron; and he said, "Thus says the LORD: 'With these you shall gore Syria until they are consumed.'"
verses.22:12: And all the prophets were prophesying likewise, saying, "Go up to Ramoth Gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king."
verses.22:13: Then the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Behold now, the words of the prophets with one mouth declare good to the king. Let your word, please, be like the word of one of them, and speak what is good."
verses.22:14: And Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, whatever the LORD says to me, that I will speak."
verses.22:15: When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall we refrain?" And he said to him, "Go up and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king."
verses.22:16: So the king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear that you speak nothing to me except truth in the name of the LORD?"
verses.22:17: Then he said, "I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his house in peace.'"
verses.22:18: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but only evil?"
verses.22:19: Then he said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting upon His throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside Him, on His right hand and on His left.
verses.22:20: And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?' And one spoke in this manner, and another spoke in that manner.
verses.22:21: Then a spirit came forth and stood before the LORD, and said, 'I will entice him.' And the LORD said to him, 'By what means?'
verses.22:22: And he said, 'I will go forth and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You shall entice him, and also prevail. Go forth and do so.'
verses.22:23: Now therefore, behold, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the LORD has spoken calamity concerning you."
verses.22:24: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah upon the cheek, and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak with you?"
verses.22:25: And Micaiah said, "Behold, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself."
verses.22:26: So the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah, and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
verses.22:27: and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this man in the prison house, and feed him bread of affliction and water of affliction, until I come in peace.'"
verses.22:28: And Micaiah said, "If you indeed return in peace, the LORD has not spoken by me." And he said, "Hear, all you peoples!"
verses.22:29: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.22:30: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and enter into the battle, but you, put on your own robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.
verses.22:31: Now the king of Syria had commanded his thirty-two captains of the chariots, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, but only with the king of Israel."
verses.22:32: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "Surely he is the king of Israel!" So they turned aside against him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.22:33: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.
verses.22:34: Now a certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the armor. So he said to the driver of his chariot, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the army, for I am wounded."
verses.22:35: And the battle mounted up that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing Syria, and he died in the evening; and the blood from the wound ran out into the hollow of the chariot.
verses.22:36: Then a cry passed through the camp as the sun was going down, saying, "Every man to his city, and every man to his own land!"
verses.22:37: So the king died and was brought to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.
verses.22:38: And the chariot was washed by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood while the harlots bathed, according to the word of the LORD which He had spoken.
verses.22:39: Now the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house which he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.22:40: So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:41: Now Jehoshaphat the son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
verses.22:42: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
verses.22:43: And he walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.22:44: Yet the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense upon the high places.
verses.22:45: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.22:46: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he showed, and how he made war, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.22:51: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father. Then Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:52: Ahaziah the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
verses.22:53: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin.
verses.22:54: And he served Baal and worshiped him, and provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done.

notes.1:9: The Stone of Zoheleth, literally meaning the Serpent's Stone or the Sliding Stone, was a landmark near the spring of En Rogel just southeast of Jerusalem.
notes.1:18: The second "and now" follows the Masoretic Hebrew text directly, whereas some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions read "and you."
notes.1:27: "Your servant" follows the Masoretic Qere singular reading; the Ketiv reads the plural "your servants."
notes.1:37: The Masoretic Qere reads the full imperfect verb form here, while the Ketiv has the shortened jussive form; both convey Benaiah's solemn wish for Solomon.
notes.1:47: "God" follows the Masoretic Qere reading, whereas the Ketiv reads "your God."
notes.2:24: The Hebrew preserves a Ketiv/Qere orthographic variant on the verb "seated me," with the Masoretic Qere reading a standard Hiphil form with first-person suffix; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.2:26: "A man deserving of death" translates the Hebrew idiom "a man of death," and "the Lord GOD" renders the covenantal divine title Adonai YHWH.
notes.2:35: The Saints Hebrew Critical Text includes here the summary of Solomon's five hundred and fifty chief officers and his thrice-yearly burnt offerings, peace offerings, and incense before the LORD, corresponding to material placed in chapter 9 in the standard Masoretic arrangement and reflected here in the 3 Kingdoms tradition.
notes.2:46: The Saints Hebrew Critical Text includes here the summary of Israel's multitude, Solomon's dominion from the River (Euphrates) to the border of Egypt, and the security of Judah and Israel from Dan to Beersheba, corresponding to material placed in chapters 4 and 5 in the standard Masoretic arrangement.
notes.3:9: Hebrew literally reads "a hearing heart," denoting a mind receptive to God's wisdom and attentive in rendering judgment; "great" translates a word literally meaning "heavy" or "weighty."
notes.3:10: Here and in verse 15, the Masoretic Text uses Adonai ("the Lord") rather than the Tetragrammaton ("the LORD").
notes.3:26: Hebrew literally reads "her compassions grew warm," a vivid idiom expressing intense maternal yearning and tenderness.
notes.4:5: Hebrew kohen ordinarily means "priest," though in royal lists it may also indicate a high court minister or counselor.
notes.4:7: The Masoretic qere reads "the one" (translated "each one") with the definite article, while the ketiv reads "one" without the article.
notes.4:8: In verses 8 through 13, five of Solomon's deputies are listed by patronymic names (literally "the son of Hur," "the son of Deker," "the son of Hesed," "the son of Abinadab," and "the son of Geber").
notes.4:16: Translated according to the Masoretic vocalization as "in Aloth"; alternatively, the Hebrew may be read as the town name Bealoth.
notes.5:2: A kor was a large dry and liquid measure, approximately two hundred and twenty liters or about six bushels.
notes.5:4: The phrase "beyond the River" designates the territory west of the Euphrates River from Tiphsah down to Gaza.
notes.5:17: Following the Qere (read form), "my feet"; the Ketiv (written form) reads "his feet," referring to David.
notes.5:24: The Hebrew text uses the variant spelling "Hirom" here and in 5:32 for Hiram, king of Tyre.
notes.6:4: The Hebrew architectural expression refers to framed windows with narrowed or recessed openings.
notes.6:5: Following the Qere (read form) here and in verses 6 and 10 for the side structure built around the temple walls.
notes.6:8: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "the middle side chamber," though some ancient versions read "the lowest."
notes.6:31: The Hebrew term rendered "five-sided" here, and "four-sided" in verse 33, may alternatively denote a fifth part and a fourth part of the wall's width.
notes.7:6: The read text (qere) supplies the definite article in "the network," whereas the written text (ketiv) omits it. The Masoretic Hebrew also literally reads "the pillars" and "on top of the pomegranates" in the first sentence.
notes.7:10: The read text (qere) gives the standard spelling for "and a line," while the written text (ketiv) preserves an older orthographic variant with the same meaning.
notes.7:22: The read text (qere) omits a superfluous conjunction on "its panels" that appears in the written text (ketiv) after "and on."
notes.7:31: The read text (qere) has "these" ("all these vessels"), whereas the written text (ketiv) reads "the tent."
notes.7:44: The Hebrew idiom literally says "from floor to floor," denoting complete cedar paneling from the floor up to the ceiling or upper beams.
notes.8:2: Ethanim is the early Hebrew name for the seventh month (later known as Tishri), when the Feast of Tabernacles was celebrated.
notes.8:6: The Hebrew debir refers to the innermost sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place.
notes.8:26: Following the Masoretic Qere (read form), "Your word" (singular, matching the singular verb); the Ketiv (written form) reads "Your words" (plural).
notes.8:31: Hebrew reads literally "and the oath comes before Your altar," denoting the accused party coming to swear a solemn oath before God at the temple altar.
notes.8:48: Following the Masoretic Qere (read form), "which I have built"; the Ketiv (written form) omits the final letter, either as a defective spelling or reading "which you have built."
notes.8:53: In this critical text, Solomon's poetic dedication saying ("The LORD said that He would dwell in the thick darkness...") stands here at the close of his prayer rather than at verses 12-13.
notes.8:65: "From the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of Egypt" marks the traditional northern and southern boundaries of the Israelite kingdom, with the two seven-day periods comprising the temple dedication and the Feast of Tabernacles.
notes.9:8: Hebrew literally reads 'shall be exalted,' understood concessively in contrast to the desolation that follows; compare 2 Chronicles 7:21.
notes.9:9: The Qere reads plural 'and bowed down,' matching the plural verbs around it, whereas the Ketiv omits the final plural letter. The closing sentence on Pharaoh's daughter and the Millo stands here in this Hebrew text, corresponding to 9:24 in the standard Masoretic order.
notes.9:13: The name Cabul plays on a Hebrew expression meaning 'as nothing' or 'good-for-nothing,' reflecting Hiram's displeasure with the cities.
notes.9:26: Red Sea translates Hebrew Yam Suph, literally 'Sea of Reeds,' referring here to the Gulf of Aqaba.
notes.10:5: Following the Masoretic vocalization, the text reads 'his burnt offering that he offered'; with a slightly different vocalization, as in 2 Chronicles 9:4, it may be rendered 'his ascent by which he went up.'
notes.10:13: Royal bounty translates the Hebrew idiom literally meaning 'according to the hand of King Solomon.'
notes.10:22: The Qere reads 'Tadmor' (Palmyra in the Syrian desert), while the Ketiv reads 'Tamar' (a site in southern Judah). This verse combines the account of Solomon's forced labor and building works (9:15, 17-22 in standard Masoretic order) with the report of his Tarshish fleet.
notes.10:28: Kue denotes ancient Cilicia in southern Anatolia, renowned for horse breeding; older translations sometimes rendered the Hebrew term as 'linen yarn' or 'a drove.'
notes.11:5: Hebrew 'al-penei ("before the face of") geographically denotes "east of," referring to the southern ridge of the Mount of Olives opposite Jerusalem.
notes.11:26: Hebrew 'ephrati ("Ephrathite") here designates an Ephraimite, matching Jeroboam's hometown of Zeredah in the territory of Ephraim.
notes.11:36: Hebrew nir ("lamp") is a royal metaphor signifying the enduring continuity of David's dynasty in Jerusalem.
notes.11:43: The Masoretic Hebrew reads wayyeshev ("he remained/dwelt"), whereas the parallel in 2 Chronicles 10:2 reads wayyashov ("he returned").
notes.12:3: Qere reads the singular verb wayyavo ("came") agreeing with Jeroboam as the lead subject, while Ketiv reads the plural wayyavo'u ("they came").
notes.12:7: Qere reads the plural wayyedabberu ("they spoke") referring to the elders, whereas Ketiv reads the singular wayyedabber ("he spoke").
notes.12:21: Qere reads the singular wayyavo ("he came") for Rehoboam's arrival in Jerusalem, while Ketiv reads the plural wayyavo'u ("they came").
notes.12:24: Qere reads the standard second-person feminine pronoun 'at ("you"), while Ketiv preserves the archaic spelling 'ati; the Hebrew phrase rendered "every male" is literally an idiom meaning "one who urinates against a wall."
notes.12:33: Qere reads millibbo ("from his own heart"), indicating Jeroboam's self-devised calendar, whereas Ketiv reads millevad ("alone/apart").
notes.13:6: The Hebrew idiom rendered implore the favor of literally means to soften or appease the face of the LORD.
notes.13:11: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts within the verse from singular his son to plural they told to their father, reflecting that multiple sons were present.
notes.13:12: The Masoretic vocalization reads the Qal verb had seen rather than a causative form meaning showed.
notes.13:33: The Hebrew phrase rendered consecrated literally means filled his hand, the standard biblical idiom for ordaining a priest.
notes.14:25: The Masoretic text presents a ketiv-qere spelling variant for the Egyptian pharaoh, with the written form Shushaq and the read form Shishaq, translated here as Shishak.
notes.14:27: The Hebrew term rendered guard literally means runners, referring to the royal footguard who escorted the king and watched the palace entrance.
notes.15:4: Hebrew nir ('lamp') signifies an enduring royal lineage preserved for David in Jerusalem.
notes.15:15: The Qere reads 'and the dedicated things of the house of the LORD'; the Ketiv reads 'and his own dedicated things [into] the house of the LORD' (cf. 2 Chronicles 15:18).
notes.15:18: The Qere supplies the definite article ('the king's house'), whereas the Ketiv omits it.
notes.16:11: Literally 'one who urinates against a wall,' an idiomatic Hebrew expression meaning a single male.
notes.16:26: The Qere reads the singular 'his sin,' whereas the Ketiv reads the plural 'his sins.'
notes.16:28: In this critical text, the notice concerning Jehoshaphat (found in the Masoretic Text at 1 Kings 22:47-50) follows Omri's burial; the Qere reads 'made' and plural 'were wrecked' where the Ketiv reads 'ten' and a singular verb.
notes.16:34: The Qere reads 'Segub,' whereas the Ketiv reads 'Segib'; the loss of Hiel's sons fulfilled Joshua's curse in Joshua 6:26.
notes.17:1: The Hebrew phrase behind 'of the settlers of Gilead' refers to resident sojourners in Gilead, indicating Elijah's origin among the inhabitants of the Transjordanian hill country.
notes.17:14: The Masoretic Qere reads the infinitive construct 'tet' ('until the day the LORD gives rain'), whereas the Ketiv has the form 'ttn'; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.17:15: The Masoretic Qere reads 'she and he' to agree with the feminine singular verb 'she ate,' whereas the Ketiv reads 'he and she'; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.18:21: The Hebrew participle rendered 'limp' vividly portrays hobbling back and forth between two divided loyalties, creating deliberate wordplay with the same verbal root used of Baal's prophets limping about the altar in verse 26.
notes.18:27: The phrase 'he has turned aside' renders a rare Hebrew noun often understood as a pointed euphemism for stepping aside to relieve oneself or being preoccupied.
notes.18:32: Two seahs of seed represents a traditional dry measure of roughly fifteen liters, indicating a trench large enough to hold a substantial volume of water.
notes.18:36: The Masoretic Qere reads the singular 'at Your word,' whereas the Ketiv reads the plural 'at Your words'; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.19:3: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "he saw," whereas some ancient versions reflect a graphically similar form meaning "he was afraid."
notes.19:4: Ketiv/Qere: the written form (ketiv) uses the feminine numeral for "one," while the read form (qere) follows the masculine numeral agreeing with the broom tree, as in verse 5.
notes.19:12: The Hebrew phrase literally means "a sound/voice of thin stillness," traditionally rendered "a still small voice."
notes.20:1: In the 3 Kingdoms chapter order followed here, the account of Naboth's vineyard appears as chapter 20 (corresponding to 1 Kings 21 in the standard Masoretic chapter division).
notes.20:8: Ketiv/Qere: the written form (ketiv) reads definite "the letters," whereas the read form (qere) followed here reads indefinite "letters."
notes.20:10: "Sons of Belial" is a Hebrew idiom for worthless or wicked men; "cursed" translates a Hebrew verb literally meaning "blessed," used as a reverent euphemism to avoid writing "curse" directly beside the name of God.
notes.20:21: "Every male" renders a blunt Hebrew idiom for every male member of the house, and "both bond and free" is a merism encompassing everyone without exception.
notes.21:1: In the Saints chapter order, which follows the sequence of 3 Kingdoms, this chapter corresponds to 1 Kings 20 in standard Masoretic numbering; the Hebrew name Aram is rendered traditionally as Syria.
notes.21:23: The Hebrew plural form may be rendered either "Their gods are gods of the hills," reflecting Syrian polytheism, or "Their God is a God of the hills," as addressed directly of the LORD in verse 28.
notes.21:33: The rare Hebrew idiom expresses the messengers eagerly seizing upon and confirming Ahab's unguarded word "brother" as a binding pledge of clemency.
notes.21:38: The rare Hebrew term apher denotes a headcloth or bandage placed over the eyes, distinct from epher ("ashes"), used here to conceal the prophet's identity.
notes.21:41: Ketiv reads the standard preposition me'al, while Qere reads the poetic form me'alei ("from over"), both conveying the same meaning.
notes.22:6: The prophets here use the Hebrew title Adonai ("the Lord") rather than the covenant name YHWH ("the LORD"), which appears in verses 12 and 15.
notes.22:13: Following the Masoretic qere ("your word," singular), which agrees with the singular verb; the ketiv reads the plural "your words."
notes.22:21: Literally "the spirit"; Hebrew commonly uses the definite article for a specific figure newly introduced into a narrative scene.
notes.22:38: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "and the harlots bathed," underscoring the ignominious fulfillment of the word of the LORD against Ahab.
